_meta.what: per pool renderer, the real Windows devices behind it and the blocklist outcome (nsIGfxInfo::GetFeatureStatus) official Firefox gives each, for zoom.stealth.gfx.feature_status
_meta.measured: 2026-11-01 and 2026-11-09, official Firefox 159.0 build 20261022150525, Windows 11 26100 declared (MOZ_GFX_SPOOF_*), every live feature of widget/GfxInfoFeatureDefs.inc, read right after startup and again later (identical)
_meta.weights: each device weighs its share of its family (`share`, Steam October 2026 for the models it covers, or the Firefox hardware report's codename) scaled so that the devices of a family add up to the family's weight in win_gpu_family_weights.json (percent). The pool draws the bucket by the sum of the weights behind it, then the device inside it by `weight`.
_meta.alu_family: NVIDIA devices only: `chip` is the chip the device id names (public PCI ID registry), `alu_family` the GPU generation of the chip (GM2xx nv_maxwell, GP10x nv_pascal, TU1xx nv_turing, GA10x nv_ampere, AD10x nv_ada, GB20x nv_blackwell). zoom.stealth.webgl.alu_class is derived from it (_webgl_personas.alu_class_for).

left_out.mtl_8826: Meteor Lake reports 'Intel(R) Arc(TM) Graphics' on most machines, which sanitizes to the Arc A750 bucket, not HD Graphics
left_out.hd3200_9001: no Windows 11 driver: a real Radeon HD 3200 runs on Microsoft Basic Display there
left_out.hd4000_5161: Ivy Bridge: a CPU Windows 11 does not support
left_out.hd520_2115: Skylake: a CPU Windows 11 does not support
left_out.cezanne_21925: same bucket and outcomes as raphael_32015 and renoir_21925; no family of its own
